items.title: Ep32. Why is moss slippy?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max explore how moss holds water like a tiny sponge, how wet surfaces reduce friction, and why algae and other microscopic organisms can make moss even more slippery. They also discover why moss loves damp places and how to stay safe on mossy paths, rocks and steps.

items.title: Ep31. How do toilets flush?
items.desc: In this episode of Little Ears, Big Ideas, Lily and Max dive into the surprisingly clever science hiding inside an everyday toilet. Discover where the flushing water comes from, how gravity helps create that powerful WHOOSH, what a siphon does, why toilets have a bendy trapway, and how the tank magically knows when to stop filling.

items.title: Ep30. Why can land animals walk, but ocean animals can't?
items.desc: In this episode of Little Ears, Big Ideas, Lily and Max explore how animals’ bodies are perfectly suited to the places they live. We’ll discover why legs are so useful on land, how fins and flippers help animals move through water

items.title: Ep29. How do earthquakes happen?
items.desc: In this episode of Little Ears, Big Ideas, Lily and Max head beneath the Earth’s surface to discover tectonic plates, faults, seismic waves and the enormous forces that can build up underground. With a simple hands-on experiment, they explore how rocks can get stuck, pressure can build, and a sudden slip can send vibrations travelling through the Earth.

items.title: Ep28. How big is the universe?
items.desc: In this episode of Little Ears, Big Ideas, Lily and Max zoom out from Earth to the Solar System, the Milky Way, and far beyond to discover just how enormous space really is.
